# Sirach Chapter 33 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 33 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_033_page_001.jpg

---

33:1 Nothing truly bad will happen to someone who fears the Lord; when tested, they will be rescued every time.

33:2 A wise person embraces God's instruction, but the hypocrite toward it is like a ship caught in a storm — at the mercy of every wave.

33:3 The discerning person trusts in God's law; for them, the law is as reliable as a sacred oracle.

33:4 Think before you speak, and people will hear you. Organize your thinking, and then respond.

33:5 A fool's mind is like a spinning cartwheel, his thoughts rolling around like an unsteady axle.

33:6 A sarcastic friend is like a stallion — he'll rear up under anyone who tries to ride him.

33:7 Why should one day be better than another, when they all share the same sunlight throughout the year?

33:8 The Lord in his wisdom made them different, establishing seasons and festivals as distinct occasions.

33:9 Some days he elevated and made holy; others he left as ordinary days.

33:10 All human beings come from the earth; Adam himself was formed from the ground.

33:11 In his great wisdom, God distinguished people from one another and set them on different paths.

33:12 Some he blessed and lifted high; some he set apart and drew close to himself. Others he cursed and lowered, uprooting them from where they stood.

33:13 We are like clay in the potter's hands — shaped however the potter pleases. Human beings are in the hands of their Maker, to be dealt with as he sees fit.

33:14 Good and evil are opposites; so are life and death. The same is true of the godly person and the sinner — they stand on opposite sides.

33:15 Look at all of God's creation: everything comes in pairs, each one opposite the other.

33:16 I myself came along last, like a gleaner working behind the grape-pickers. But through God's blessing I moved ahead, and like a vintner I filled my wine vat.

33:17 Remember that I haven't done this work just for myself — it's for everyone who seeks to learn.

33:18 Listen to me, leaders of the people, rulers of the assembly — pay attention.

33:19 While you are alive, do not hand over your authority to a son, wife, brother, or friend. And don't give away your property while you can still use it — otherwise you'll regret it and have to beg for it back.

33:20 As long as there's breath in your body, don't let anyone take your place.

33:21 It's much better for your children to depend on you than for you to be dependent on them.

33:22 Stay in charge of your own affairs. Don't let anyone tarnish your reputation.

33:23 When your final days arrive, at the moment of death, then distribute what you have.

33:24 A donkey needs fodder, a stick, and a load to carry. A servant needs food, discipline, and work.

33:25 Keep your servant busy and you'll get your rest. Let him sit idle and he'll start thinking about freedom.

33:26 A yoke and a harness will tame a stubborn neck; for a dishonest servant, sterner measures are needed.

33:27 Give him work so that he has no time to be lazy — idleness teaches all kinds of trouble.

33:28 Put him to work as his situation requires; and if he won't cooperate, tighten his constraints.

33:29 But don't be excessive with anyone; always act with discernment.

33:30 If you have a servant, treat him like a member of the family — after all, you've paid good money for him.

33:31 If you mistreat him and he runs away, what will you do then? Where will you go to find him?

33:32 Every path in life leads somewhere — the honorable and the shameful. For the upright, there's always a way to make things right.

33:33 My own heart takes joy in wisdom's teaching, and I say so without any embarrassment.
